instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires periodic expense statements to be filed by registered principals on Jan. 31 and July 31, not an annual lobbyist spending report.
No provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; spending reports are filed by principals semiannually and lobbyists may not lobby unless licensed/authorized.
The only periodic spending disclosure required in the provided text is the principal’s semiannual expense statement, so there is no separate 'other' frequency lobbyist spending report.
The statute does not require quarterly lobbyist spending reports; it requires principals to file on or before July 31 and January 31.
The semiannual spending report is filed by the registered principal, while the lobbyist only supplies information to the principal for that statement.
No tri-annual, legislative-calendar-linked lobbyist spending report is specified; the statute sets principal filings for Jan. 31 and July 31.
Itemization requirements in §13.68 apply to the principal’s expense statement, not to a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Wisconsin requires principals (not lobbyists) to file semiannual expense statements, with lobbyists only providing signed information to the principal, so lobbyists file no separate spending report.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/topics is a reporting obligation of the principal to the board, not a lobbyist’s separate periodic report.
Compensation to lobbyists is reported by the principal in its expense statement, while the lobbyist does not file a separate compensation disclosure report.
The principal’s expense statement requires time records and certain reimbursements but does not impose a lobbyist-filed contact-disclosure report.
Issue-level allocation (10%+ time spent by topic) is required in the principal’s expense statement, not as lobbyist expenditure-per-issue reporting.
General issues/topics of lobbying must be reported by the principal to the board, and the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed issue report.
Reporting of general subjects (topics) of lobbying is a principal’s obligation under §13.67(1), not a separate lobbyist spending report requirement.
While the principal must report certain expenditures (e.g., travel/living expenses), the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate report of gifts/entertainment/transport/lodging.
Indirect lobbying costs are disclosed in the principal’s expense statement, and lobbyists are not designated as separate periodic spending-report filers.

The statute requires itemized/allocated disclosures by principals and only requires lobbyists to provide signed information to principals, so lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports.

The lobbyist license application must include the lobbyist’s social security number, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate spending report disclosing their address and phone number.
Bill/rule/topic identification is reported by the principal and not via a lobbyist’s periodic activity/spending report.
Nature of the principal’s business/purposes is disclosed on the principal’s registration statement, not on a lobbyist-filed spending report.

The principal registration statement requires the principal’s business address, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose principals’ address and phone number in a separate lobbyist spending report.
While authorizations link lobbyists to principals, the statute does not impose a lobbyist-filed periodic report listing all principals represented.
Reporting specific bill numbers/proposed rule numbers is required of the principal under §13.67(1), not in a lobbyist’s separate report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation to lobbyists are components of the principal’s expense statement, not a lobbyist’s own spending report.
Aggregate total lobbying expenditures are reported by the principal in its expense statement, and no separate lobbyist total-expenditure report is required.

Because Wisconsin assigns periodic spending disclosure to the principal (with lobbyists supplying information), there is no lobbyist requirement to file itemized spending reports including both issues/bills and compensation.
The law contains no lobbyist periodic spending report at all, so it does not impose a lobbyist 'no-activity' report requirement.

The statute provides an exception for furnishing items of pecuniary value to a relative or household member, and does not require lobbyists to report spending on household members of public officials in a lobbyist spending report.
Itemized formats described in §13.68 apply to the principal’s expense statement, and there is no lobbyist-filed spending report to be itemized.
